newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's rating shows economy is improving.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's rating shows economy is improving.

text.p: The upgrading of Hungary's long-term foreign currency rating by IBCA on Tuesday underscored the country's economic progress, the central bank president and analysts said.
"Both the markets and the rating agencies reflect that the Hungarian economy is moving in the right direction," Gyorgy Suranyi, president of the National Bank of Hungary, told Reuters.
"This is true for external processes and shows that the economic growth is picking up in a way that the external accounts are moving to the right direction as well."

Europe's IBCA rating agency announced that it had upgraded Hungary's long-term foreign currency rating to BBB from BBB-. It said that "Hungary's external debt position since 1994 is unparalleled in any rate emerging market in recent times".
"It's a reinforcement of the positive attitude since the market was expecting that upgrade to happen soon," said Sara Zervos, emerging market strategist at BZW in London.

"Basically, since Hungary is finally seeing results from its austerity package," she said. "The economy has turned around and it's giving the rating agencies a good reason to reanalyse their credit standing."

IBCA's decision follows an upgrade by Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co to BBB from BBB- of Hungary's foreign currency obligations earlier this month, and Suranyi said he hoped other rating agencies will follow.

"I hope that this process...may continue later this year and other rating agencies will take into consideration the developments of the past 12 months, which may found an improvement in our (Hungary's) rating by others as well."
In 1996 IBCA was the first to assign Hungary an investment grade rating.
Nevertheless, another analyst said the timing of the upgrade was a little surprising.
"It has come slightly earlier than we expected," said David Mars, analyst at SBC Warburg in London, adding they expected Hungary's next upgrade by September or October.
Mars said Hungary's most important rating occurred last year when IBCA upgraded the country to the investment grade.

"That's the biggest step and any further upgrades are less important than that," Mars said. "It (the current upgrade) is going to be positive but mildly positive because the market is already fully aware of the fundamentals which IBCA has made its assessment on."
